title: Quiet Clues: checking AI-written deduction puzzles beyond a unique solution (free browser demo)
author: Sott1987
selftext:
Quiet Clues is a small experiment in using an AI assistant to build fixed, text-based deduction mysteries. I own the project and commissioned the work; the assistant created the stories, puzzle logic and code, and prepared this post with my permission. No AI runs while you play.



The useful development detail is the separation between checking the puzzle model and checking the reading experience. The validation enumerated the possible assignments against each case's encoded clue constraints and found exactly one solution for each of the three cases. The English and Russian clues and solutions were also compared with the downloadable PDFs so that the browser and print versions describe the same puzzle.



Those checks have a blind spot: a unique solution in the encoded model does not establish that a reader will interpret the prose the same way. They also say nothing about whether a deduction feels satisfying or a hint reveals too much. We have technical QA, but no substantive reader feedback yet, so I would not call the cases playtested.



The free sampler is here: [https://quiet-clues-alderwick.sott1987.chatgpt.site/?source=reddit\_aigamedev\_workflow](https://quiet-clues-alderwick.sott1987.chatgpt.site/?source=reddit_aigamedev_workflow)



There are three gentle village mysteries in English and Russian, optional hints and large-print PDFs. No murder themes, timer, account, installation or payment. Adult volunteers, especially people new to deduction games, are welcome to try only the first case, The Borrowed Key. Where did a clue feel ambiguous, what made you open a hint, and would you want another case? An honest comment or the on-page feedback form is enough; criticism is welcome and there is no payment or review exchange.



For developers working on similar games: how do you test whether natural-language clues match the formal constraints without turning the story into a list of equations? That gap is the next thing this project needs to resolve.
